questions.stem: A nurse performing telephone triage receives a caller who wants a definitive diagnosis. What is the nurse's most appropriate role?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Give a definitive diagnosis from the symptom list alone because telephone triage protocols are intended to replace a complete medical evaluation by a clinician.","B":"Use structured assessment, clinical judgment, and decision-support tools to determine the urgency and appropriate level of care, while documenting the encounter.","C":"Avoid documenting the call because telephone triage recommendations are informal and do not become part of the clinical information used for follow-up care.","D":"Follow the written algorithm mechanically without considering clinical judgment, because deviations based on patient-specific information are unsafe in telephone triage."}}
questions.rationale: Telephone triage is professional nursing practice rather than remote medical diagnosis. AAACN emphasizes systematic assessment, critical thinking, clinical judgment, appropriate use of decision-support tools, and documentation. Option B accurately describes that role.
questions.source_name: American Academy of Ambulatory Care Nursing — Telephone Triage as Professional Nursing Practice
questions.source_detail: AAACN describes telephone triage as full-scope professional nursing requiring structured assessment, critical thinking, clinical judgment, decision-support tools, and documentation.

questions.stem: A client wants another medical opinion before proceeding with a major elective operation. Which nursing response is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Discourage another opinion because requesting one indicates loss of trust and may justify ending the current therapeutic relationship before surgery is scheduled.","B":"Tell the client that second opinions are reserved for situations in which the treating clinician formally requests consultation from another specialist.","C":"Support the client's decision to seek a second opinion and help clarify how records or referrals can be obtained, while noting possible health-plan requirements.","D":"Advise the client to proceed with the planned operation first because obtaining a second opinion after treatment avoids unnecessary delay in the current plan."}}
questions.rationale: AMA ethics guidance recognizes the patient's ability to seek a second opinion. Option C supports autonomy and practical coordination without implying that all insurance plans cover the same services or that a second opinion is mandatory.
questions.source_name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics — Consultation, Referral & Second Opinions
questions.source_detail: AMA ethics guidance states that patients may seek a second opinion and physicians should assure patients of that option while noting applicable health-plan restrictions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a durable power of attorney for health care?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It authorizes the named agent to manage the person's financial accounts but does not provide authority to participate in medical decision-making if capacity is lost.","B":"It names a health care proxy who can make health care decisions if the person cannot communicate or decide, subject to the document and applicable state law.","C":"It is a physician DNR order specifying which resuscitation measures should be withheld if cardiac or respiratory arrest occurs during an emergency.","D":"It transfers all legal decision-making authority immediately after signing, even while the person retains decision-making capacity and can communicate preferences."}}
questions.rationale: A durable power of attorney for health care names a health care proxy who can make health care decisions if the person cannot communicate or make them. Option B is correct; the document is distinct from financial power of attorney and from a DNR order, and state rules vary.
questions.source_name: National Institute on Aging — Advance Care Planning: Advance Directives for Health Care
questions.source_detail: NIA explains that a durable power of attorney for health care names a health care proxy who can make health care decisions if the person cannot communicate their own wishes; state rules vary.

questions.stem: A client has a do-not-resuscitate (DNR) order. Which statement correctly explains its scope?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The order means routine medications, nutrition, symptom treatment, and nursing care should be stopped because the client has declined further medical treatment.","B":"The order means the client should receive comfort measures only and cannot receive disease-directed treatment even when that treatment remains consistent with goals.","C":"The order directs clinicians not to perform CPR if breathing or heartbeat stops; it does not by itself instruct them to withhold other treatments or pain medicine.","D":"The order applies only to chest compressions, while defibrillation, emergency ventilation, and resuscitation drugs should still be provided during cardiac arrest."}}
questions.rationale: A DNR is specific to cardiopulmonary resuscitation when breathing or heartbeat stops. It does not by itself discontinue medications, nutrition, pain treatment, or other care. Option C accurately states its scope.
questions.source_detail: MedlinePlus states that a DNR instructs providers not to perform CPR if breathing or heartbeat stops and is specific to CPR, not other treatments such as pain medicine or nutrition.

questions.stem: An incapacitated client has a court-appointed guardian whose order expressly includes authority for routine health care decisions. A sibling demands to decide instead. What should the nurse do?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Direct routine health care decisions to the legally authorized guardian within the scope of the court order, while involving the client as much as remaining capacity allows.","B":"Accept the sibling as decision-maker because frequent family involvement automatically overrides authority formally granted to a court-appointed guardian for health care decisions.","C":"Ignore the guardianship order because court-appointed guardians can address placement or finances but can never be authorized to participate in medical decisions.","D":"Ask whichever relative is physically present to decide because legal authority is unnecessary once a client has been documented as lacking decision-making capacity."}}
questions.rationale: Because the scenario expressly states that the court order grants the guardian authority for routine health care decisions, the nurse should direct those decisions to that legally authorized guardian within the order's scope while involving the client to the extent possible. Authority varies by state and court order.
questions.source_name: NIH/PubMed — Medical decision-making during the guardianship process for incapacitated, hospitalized adults
questions.source_detail: Published evidence describes court-appointed guardians acting as legally authorized surrogate decision-makers for incapacitated adults; the extent of authority depends on the court order and state law.

questions.stem: A nurse manager is developing staffing for critically ill patients. Which principle is most consistent with current critical-care staffing standards?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Critically ill patients generally require about one nurse for every one to two patients, with assignments adjusted for acuity, workload, care needs, and nurse competency.","B":"Critical-care assignments should routinely use the same patient load as a general medical-surgical unit because monitoring technology offsets the higher patient acuity.","C":"Every critically ill patient requires permanent one-to-one nursing regardless of acuity, stability, therapies, workload, or the competency and current experience of available nursing staff.","D":"A fixed national ratio alone determines every assignment, so patient condition, workload, care complexity, and nurse competency should not modify staffing decisions."}}
questions.rationale: AACN critical-care staffing standards anticipate that critically ill patients generally require about one nurse for every two patients, with assignment decisions also reflecting acuity, workload, and nurse competency. Option A captures both the baseline and the need for individualized staffing.
questions.source_name: American Association of Critical-Care Nurses — Critical Care Staffing Standards
questions.source_detail: AACN states that critically ill or injured patients generally require about one nurse to two patients, with staffing also matching patient needs and nurse competencies.

questions.stem: A client is diagnosed with acute compartment syndrome of the lower leg. Which treatment should the nurse anticipate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Elevation alone above heart level until swelling resolves because acute compartment syndrome generally improves without surgical pressure release when perfusion is reduced.","B":"Urgent surgical decompression with fasciotomy to relieve compartment pressure and reduce the risk of irreversible nerve and muscle injury from prolonged ischemia.","C":"A tighter circumferential cast to reduce edema because increasing external pressure restores capillary perfusion within the affected muscle compartment during the emergency.","D":"Observe and give oral analgesics until pain resolves because definitive surgery is reserved for chronic exertional compartment syndrome, not acute cases."}}
questions.rationale: Acute compartment syndrome is a surgical emergency. Fasciotomy releases the fascia and relieves dangerous compartment pressure before prolonged ischemia causes irreversible nerve and muscle damage. Option B is correct.
questions.source_name: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons — Acute Compartment Syndrome
questions.source_detail: AAOS identifies acute compartment syndrome as a surgical emergency requiring rapid pressure relief; surgical incisions through skin and fascia relieve dangerous compartment pressure.

questions.stem: A client with diabetic ketoacidosis has a serum potassium concentration of 3.0 mmol/L before insulin is started. Which treatment sequence is expected?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Begin intravenous insulin immediately without potassium replacement because insulin will raise extracellular potassium as ketoacidosis begins to resolve during treatment.","B":"Give a potassium-wasting diuretic before insulin because lowering potassium further reduces the risk of arrhythmia when glucose enters cells during DKA therapy.","C":"Withhold fluids and potassium until insulin normalizes glucose because electrolyte replacement before glycemic correction increases the risk of cerebral edema.","D":"Begin potassium replacement and delay insulin until potassium rises above 3.5 mmol/L, because insulin can lower serum potassium further and provoke serious arrhythmias."}}
questions.rationale: With DKA and potassium below 3.5 mmol/L, current consensus guidance recommends potassium replacement and delaying insulin until potassium exceeds 3.5 mmol/L. Starting insulin at 3.0 mmol/L can worsen hypokalemia and precipitate life-threatening arrhythmias or respiratory muscle weakness.
questions.source_name: ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS — Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report
questions.source_detail: The 2024 consensus report recommends potassium replacement when admission potassium is below 3.5 mmol/L and delaying insulin until potassium rises above 3.5 mmol/L.

questions.stem: Which finding most strongly favors serotonin syndrome over neuroleptic malignant syndrome in a client with hyperthermia and altered mental status?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Generalized bradyreflexia with marked lead-pipe rigidity developing over several days after exposure to a dopamine-blocking medication used for psychosis.","B":"Hyperreflexia and inducible or spontaneous clonus developing rapidly after exposure to a serotonergic medication or a clinically important medication change.","C":"Profound flaccid paralysis without tremor, clonus, hyperreflexia, or rigidity after a medication change involving both serotonergic and antipsychotic agents.","D":"Isolated fever without neuromuscular abnormalities because serotonin syndrome is distinguished from NMS mainly by the absence of abnormal reflexes or muscle activity."}}
questions.rationale: Serotonin syndrome usually has neuromuscular hyperreactivity, especially hyperreflexia and clonus, and often develops rapidly after a serotonergic exposure or change. NMS more often features marked rigidity and a slower onset. Option B is the best discriminator.
questions.source_detail: Serotonin syndrome is characterized by neuromuscular hyperreactivity including hyperreflexia and clonus, whereas NMS more typically produces a slowed neuromuscular response with rigidity.

questions.stem: After treatment for anaphylaxis, the client's symptoms have fully resolved. Why may continued observation still be appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Anaphylaxis can recur as a biphasic reaction after initial resolution, so observation should be individualized according to episode severity, treatment needs, and risk factors.","B":"Every patient must remain hospitalized for the same fixed period because biphasic reactions occur at a predictable time regardless of episode severity or treatment response.","C":"Recurrence is possible only after another exposure to the allergen, so observation is unnecessary once symptoms resolve if the trigger has been removed from the environment.","D":"Observation is needed mainly to confirm that epinephrine has been eliminated because residual epinephrine itself commonly causes a second anaphylactic episode after clinical recovery."}}
questions.rationale: A biphasic anaphylactic reaction can occur after apparent initial resolution. Continued observation can therefore be appropriate, but the duration should be individualized rather than assumed to be identical for every patient. Option A reflects current risk-based practice.
questions.source_detail: AAAAI notes that anaphylaxis symptoms can resolve and later return, and recommends emergency evaluation and monitoring after anaphylaxis; observation is individualized according to clinical course and risk.
